body: @claude summarize in a comment the exact change this issue calls for — which functions in scripts/translate.py leak file handles, and the minimal fix shape. Comment only; do not open a PR. (Live smoke test of the newly-wired Claude workflow.)

**Claude finished @hsb3's task in 51s** —— [View job](https://github.com/hsb3/dotfiles-agents/actions/runs/28588469651)

---
### Summary: file-handle leaks in `scripts/translate.py`

- [x] Read `scripts/translate.py` and enumerate every unclosed file handle
- [x] Locate the `-W ignore::ResourceWarning` suppression in the `Makefile`
- [x] Post the summary comment (no PR — comment-only smoke test)

This is analysis only, per the trigger request — no code was changed and no PR was opened.

#### Functions that leak file handles

Every one of these opens a file without a `with` block, so the handle is only closed when the GC gets to it — the source of the `ResourceWarning`s the tests currently hit:

| # | Location | Leaking call |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `parse_roster` — `translate.py:56` | `for raw in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):` |
| 2 | `parse_externals` — `translate.py:84` | `for raw in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):` |
| 3 | `parse_plugins` — `translate.py:109` | `for raw in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):` |
| 4 | `parse_capabilities` — `translate.py:125` | `for raw in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):` |
| 5 | `parse_cma_options` — `translate.py:146` | `for raw in open(path, encoding="utf-8"):` |
| 6 | `sha256_path` — `translate.py:174` | `h.update(open(path, "rb").read())` |
| 7 | `sha256_path` — `translate.py:185` | `h.update(open(fp, "rb").read())` (inside the sorted-items loop) |
| 8 | `transform_agent_opencode` — `translate.py:193` | `text = open(src_path, encoding="utf-8").read()` |
| 9 | `agent_system` — `translate.py:215` | `text = open(src_path, encoding="utf-8").read()` |
| 10 | `skill_display_title` — `translate.py:226` | `text = open(skill_md, encoding="utf-8").read()` |
| 11 | `load_mcp_spec` — `translate.py:239` | `json.load(open(src_path, encoding="utf-8"))` |
| 12 | `build()` (opencode agent write) — `translate.py:444` | `open(os.path.join(out_root, d), "w").write(transform_agent_opencode(src))` |
| 13 | `diff_trees` — `translate.py:622` | `open(fa[rel], "rb").read() != open(fb[rel], "rb").read()` (two handles) |
| 14 | `main()` `--check` — `translate.py:647` | `json.load(open(root_mp))` |
| 15 | `main()` `--check` — `translate.py:651` | `json.load(open(RESULTS))` |

Note: `translate.py:337` (`open(...).close()` for `.gitkeep`) already closes synchronously and does **not** warn — no fix needed there, though it could be normalized for consistency.

Everywhere the code already uses `with open(...) as fh:` (`write_json`, `write_root_marketplace`, the plugin/marketplace/CMA JSON writers, `write_results`) is already correct and untouched.

#### Minimal fix shape

Two repeated patterns cover 13 of the 15 sites, so a pair of tiny helpers near the top of the file removes the duplication cleanly:

```python
def read_text(path):
    with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh:
        return fh.read()

def read_bytes(path):
    with open(path, "rb") as fh:
        return fh.read()
```

- Sites 8–10 (`.read()` with `encoding="utf-8"`) → `read_text(path)`.
- Sites 6, 7, 13 (`"rb"` + `.read()`) → `read_bytes(path)`.
- Site 11 (`json.load(open(...))`) → `json.loads(read_text(path))`, or a `with` block if `json.load(fh)` is preferred.
- Sites 14, 15 (`json.load(open(...))` guarded by `os.path.exists`) → same as above.
- Sites 1–5 (`for raw in open(path, ...):`) iterate line-by-line, so they don't fit `read_text` as cleanly — wrap each in `with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as fh: for raw in fh:` (keeping the existing loop body indented one level deeper), rather than forcing them through the helper.
- Site 12 (a single write-then-immediately-read-elsewhere) → `with open(..., "w") as fh: fh.write(...)`.

This is a pure resource-handling refactor — no output/behavior change, so `targets/` stays byte-identical and `make ci`'s drift guard stays green.

#### Part B — drop the suppression

`Makefile:23`:
```
@python3 -W ignore::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -q
```
Once all 15 sites above are wrapped, this becomes:
```
@python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -t . -q
```

Acceptance check from the issue (`python3 -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`) should then pass with zero warnings.
